thesis: A self-serve, low-cost regulatory incident-reporting clock and done-for-you security program for small and mid-size firms facing NIS2 ("important entities"), the FTC Safeguards Rule and SEC rules for small firms, likely sold through MSSPs and MSPs. The only gap rated crowdedness 2/3, and a compliance-driven market of the kind the backtest shows the method can find.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Enterprise decisioning tools (RadarFirst, BreachRx, OneTrust) quote-only; no self-serve product for small NIS2 or FTC-covered firms
Enterprise GRC offers NIS2 three-stage BSI reporting only as add-on or configuration, not ready workflow
Multi-regime triage (NIS2, DORA, Reg S-P, FTC) at one incident: hundreds of concurrent obligations overwhelm processes
No tool drafts filings straight into national portals; BSI portal submissions are manual via ELSTER-based accounts

market_research.wtp_evidence: Enterprises buy quote-only tools (BreachRx: 100+ customers incl. Amex, Coinbase; $15M Series A in May 2025); SMB NIS2 platforms start ~EUR 10,000.
market_research.bundling_note: Cloud providers don't give away jurisdictional notification logic, but GRC/privacy suites (OneTrust, ServiceNow, NIS2 compliance platforms) and MDR/incident-response retainers bundle reporting, and authorities run free portals.
market_research.summary: Established enterprise tools and notification services exist; the opening is a self-serve, low-cost multi-regime reporting clock for SMB and mid-market firms (NIS2 'important entities', FTC-covered non-banks, small RIAs/broker-dealers), likely sold via MSSPs/MDR.

threat.reason: Post-incident regulatory reporting and notification; no effect on attacker behaviour.

paid_market_gaps.gap: SOC 2 platforms start around $8.5k-$15k/year before a $10k-$50k audit; unaffordable for sub-10-person firms handling low-risk data
No-IT micro businesses and nonprofits lack a guided, done-for-you program; platforms assume an engineer to integrate and remediate
Awareness training priced from 25-seat bands and 3-year terms; Microsoft phishing simulation locked to E5/Defender Plan 2
SaaS vendors gate SSO behind enterprise tiers, inflating small-company security costs 3x-10x

market_research.wtp_evidence: Buyers pay public list prices: SOC 2/ISO platforms $4,500-$8,500 per 12 months on AWS Marketplace, Cyber Essentials from £320+VAT, awareness training $2.40/seat/month at 25-50 seats (3-year term).
market_research.bundling_note: Clouds don't bundle SOC 2 automation, but governments give free prep (NCSC action plan, CISA scanning) and Microsoft bundles training in higher tiers.
market_research.summary: Crowded, well-funded compliance-automation and training markets serve funded startups; the opening is a cheap, done-for-you program for sub-20-person firms and nonprofits without IT, likely sold through MSPs or bundled with certification.

threat.reason: Broad small-business audits and training; general hygiene with no specific technique link among candidates.

flagged_claims.claim: Vendor Vanta: no rate card on site; Essentials $14,000 / Plus $21,500 / Professional $23,000 (1-20 employees); audit extra
flagged_claims.issue: The AWS prices are correct. But the same listing says to 'preview pricing for 1-20 employees and more at vanta.com/pricing', which contradicts 'no rate card on site'. Nothing on the page says the audit costs extra.

flagged_claims.claim: Vendor RadarFirst: incident decisioning incl. SEC materiality; segment enterprise
flagged_claims.issue: The cited Capterra page lists typical users as freelancers, small businesses, mid-size businesses and enterprises. It does not mention SEC materiality. 'Contact vendor' pricing is supported.

The only source is SECJUR's own blog, stating its own product costs 'ab 10.000 Euro' for the German Mittelstand. It is one vendor's self-reported price, not evidence of where SMB NIS2 platforms in general start.
